subject: Post-call recap: inference compatibility & next experiments
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
To: Ari Gold <ari.gold@versatech.com>, eng@versatech.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: inference compatibility & next experiments

Thanks again for the call this morning, Ari — good discussion. Quick recap + proposed next experiments so we keep momentum.

Key takeaways (what we heard)
- Primary asks: deterministic structured outputs for billing extraction, reliable streaming for live-assist, and tool/function-calling parity with your current hyperscaler integration.
- P50 latency target: <= 120ms for short-turn interactions (<= 256 tokens).
- Compliance: audit logs and private VPC deployment are checkboxes for procurement.

Proposed quick experiments (3–5 day sprint)
1) Streaming parity probe: run simultaneous streaming session (Redwood hosted) vs your hyperscaler endpoint with the same prompt set; measure tokens/sec, first-byte latency, and reconnection behavior (we will record).
2) Function-calling conformance: submit our function schema for 5 canonical ops (create_invoice, extract_line_items) and verify schema-first responses + fallback behavior when function not invoked.
3) Structured-output validator: use your existing JSON schema for billing and run 1000 synthetic bills through both systems; compute strict schema compliance and field-level diffs.
4) Performance sweep: 128/256/512 token sequences with batching off/on to observe latency vs throughput trade-offs.

Deliverables we will send by EOD tomorrow:
- parity-checklist.xlsx (attached) with test cases + acceptance criteria
- demo-recording.mp4 (short recording of streaming behavior)
- Drive folder with scripts and sample prompts (share link once uploaded)

Asks for VersaTech
- A primary API key for the hyperscaler endpoint (read-only/test) or a short script that hits it so we can run apples-to-apples calls.
- The JSON schema you use for billing extraction (or a representative sample).
- A 45-minute window Friday to run the streaming side-by-side (suggest 10:00–10:45 PT).

Next steps
- We'll schedule the streaming session and share the Drive link by EOD tomorrow.
- Marissa will own the function-calling compatibility tests; Evelyn will lead the structured-output batch runs.

Thanks — talk soon.

--

Thanks, Nikhil — that plan looks good. A few clarifications: 

- We can provide a time-limited API key for our hyperscaler test endpoint; I'll send it to your security alias (sensitive channel).
- Attached is the billing JSON schema (we'll drop it in the Drive folder) — for privacy reasons we can provide synthetic but schema-identical payloads.
- Friday 10:00–10:45 PT works for our infra lead (Sam). Please include a short pre-checklist so Sam knows what ports/endpoints to expect.

One ask from our side: when you run the function-calling probe, can you include a forced-failure case where the model returns overlapping fields (e.g., subtotal vs line_total) so we can evaluate your fallback mapping logic? That was a pain point with our prior vendor.

Appreciate the fast turnaround. I look forward to the parity checklist and the recording.

Looping in for visibility / quick handoff notes.

Evelyn — please prioritize the structured-output sweep. Steps below:
- Use the attached parity-checklist.xlsx (tab: billing-schema) and run 1k synthetic payloads.
- Measure: strict JSON-schema pass rate, field-level Levenshtein for string fields, and number of manual corrections needed.
- Flag if >2% of invoices need manual intervention.

I'll own the function-calling tests. Test plan highlights:
- 5 function schemas (create_invoice, refund, list_line_items, apply_discount, validate_tax)
- For each: run 200 calls, include 20 forced-failure cases (overlapping fields / missing params) to validate our fallback mapping and logging behavior.
- Capture structured logs + debug traces.

Nikhil — I'll prep the short pre-checklist for Sam and post the Drive link by EOD.
